nodes.title: Using the shared smooth complex realization
nodes.statement: Import the single complex-point topology and analytification of ComplexComparison PR196 Layers 0–2. For a smooth separated finite-type complex scheme X of pure dimension n, use its smooth specialization as the native n-dimensional complex analytic manifold on the actual set X(C)=Hom over Spec C from Spec C to X. Identify its local coordinates from a closed smooth affine presentation p(u,v)=0 with the u-coordinates furnished by the local inverse of (u,v) mapped to (u,p(u,v)), when the v-Jacobian is invertible. The topology, atlas independence, analytic functoriality, open-immersion comparison and etale local biholomorphisms are supplier outputs, not new constructions here. In these coordinates the analytic differential is the evaluated algebraic Jacobian, and regular functions have the same values and zero sets. Apply this interface to the existing SNC chart theorem without constructing a separate smooth analytification carrier.
hypotheses: X is smooth, separated and finite type over C; fix its pure dimension n. Work componentwise for the finitely many dimensions of a smooth scheme. The empty scheme and n=0 are included.
Points and all scheme maps commute with the C-structure maps. A prime-ideal point or an arbitrary unbased Spec C morphism is not the point carrier.
For the etale assertion the chosen local algebraic Jacobian is an isomorphism; no global injectivity of an etale morphism is assumed.
proofSteps: Import PR196 Layers 0–2 through the explicit A0-extension integration request. Use its actual over-C points, presentation-independent classical topology, analytic morphism functor and smooth native manifold specialization. Do not reconstruct their carriers or gluing.

For coordinate compatibility, import R09.7/regular-coordinates and use a closed affine presentation, locally cut out by p(u,v)=0 with invertible v-Jacobian. Its complex Jacobian gives the invertible linear term of F(u,v)=(u,p(u,v)); the native analytic inverse theorem identifies the supplier chart with its u-coordinate model.

Regular coordinate functions are polynomial quotients with denominators nonzero on their domains. Their evaluations are analytic and their derivatives are the evaluated Jacobian. Supplier functoriality identifies these formulas with the actual maps on points.

Use the supplier open-immersion and etale local-biholomorphism comparisons on this same carrier. For a regular function h, evaluation vanishes precisely when the point factors through V(h); this identifies the algebraic boundary support and analytic zero set without coherent GAGA.
acceptance: The topology is on complex-valued points, not the Zariski space of X.
Both directions of a coordinate change are analytic over C; a real smooth inverse alone is insufficient.
The statement applies to arbitrary dimension and supplies only the smooth coordinate case needed here.
All seven API clauses and four checks use the single imported PR196 smooth carrier; no independently constructed smooth analytification is substituted.

api.name: smoothComplexPoints.points
api.statement: The underlying set is exactly the over-C point set X(C); a map f acts by composition with f.

api.name: smoothComplexPoints.affineChart
api.statement: For a closed embedding of a smooth affine scheme in A^N, the imported topology agrees with the Euclidean topology on its polynomial zero locus, and the local u-coordinates are inverse-function charts. For a locally closed presentation, retain its open nonvanishing conditions as well as its equations.

api.name: smoothComplexPoints.independent
api.statement: The identity of X(C) identifies the topologies and maximal compatible analytic atlases obtained from two affine covers or presentations.

api.name: smoothComplexPoints.map
api.statement: Every C-morphism between smooth schemes induces an analytic map. The maps for identity and composition are the actual identity and composite on points.

api.name: smoothComplexPoints.openImmersion
api.statement: An algebraic open immersion j:U into X gives a biholomorphism U(C) onto its image with the induced analytic structure and an open embedding on underlying topological spaces.

api.name: smoothComplexPoints.etaleCoordinates
api.statement: An etale coordinate map is locally biholomorphic, with complex derivative the evaluated algebraic Jacobian; it need not be globally one-to-one.

api.name: smoothComplexPoints.zeroSet
api.statement: For a regular function h on an algebraic open W, its analytic evaluation vanishes at a precisely when the C-point a factors through V(h); locally a Cartier equation therefore has the expected analytic support.

tests.name: SmoothComplexPointsChecks.point
tests.statement: For Spec C the over-C point set is a singleton and its analytic dimension is zero. For the empty smooth scheme the point set and atlas domains are empty.

tests.name: SmoothComplexPointsChecks.principalOpen
tests.statement: For A^1_C the realization is C with its usual topology. The inclusion D(t)=G_m into A^1 becomes C minus {0} into C; t and t inverse become z and 1/z on their respective domains.

tests.name: SmoothComplexPointsChecks.etaleSheets
tests.statement: The map G_m to G_m, z mapped to z^2, has derivative 2z and is locally biholomorphic everywhere; 1 and -1 have the same image. The API must not produce a global inverse.

tests.name: SmoothComplexPointsChecks.scalarStructure
tests.statement: The ring automorphism conjugating C induces an abstract scheme automorphism of Spec C but does not commute with the identity structure map to Spec C. It is excluded from the over-C point/map API; conjugation on C is not a complex analytic coordinate map.

uses.how: Identifies the smooth-point, open-restriction and etale-Jacobian sub-interface of its A0-extension request with the existing PR196 carrier; it does not move ownership of analytification.

nodes.title: Borel source charts on the prescribed open
nodes.statement: Let U be a smooth quasi-projective finite-type variety over a characteristic-zero field k. Import R09.7/snc-compactification to obtain a chosen smooth projective X, a dense open immersion j:U into X and a finite labelled reduced strict-SNC boundary D with complement exactly j(U). Over C, equip U and X with the smooth complex realization. For each a in X(C), choose the existing R09.7/analytic-polydisc chart c_a:N_a to P_a, centered at a, with n=dim_a X and b incident boundary labels enumerated by the first b coordinates. Here P_a is the native product of discs |z_i|<rho_i with every rho_i>0, and P_a^circ consists of its points with z_i nonzero for i<b. Export the unique biholomorphism ell_a:P_a^circ to j_an inverse-image of N_a such that j_an composed with ell_a equals c_a inverse on P_a^circ. Retain the same algebraic j, the boundary labels and the full unpunctured chart. These maps give local source charts for any analytic map on the original U. For a field embedding k into C the same conclusion applies after scalar extension of the chosen model; choosing such an embedding is an extra input.
hypotheses: U is smooth, quasi-projective and finite type over char-zero k; projectivity of X is retained from the projective closure and projective blowup chain.
Analytic assertions are over C (or after a specified embedding k into C). The algebraic existence assertion does not require such an embedding.
Boundary labels refer to globally smooth effective Cartier components with distinct incident germs. Each analytic neighbourhood avoids every nonincident component.
proofSteps: Use the existing R09.7/snc-compactification construction and its open, boundary and projective API without re-running resolution. Its R09.1 projective-closure request remains an explicit supplier obligation. Each modification is an isomorphism on the prescribed U, so j identifies that U, not a replacement birational open.

Use the imported smooth realization through smooth-complex-points to identify the analytic image of j with X(C) minus the union of the analytic boundary zero sets. For R09.7/analytic-polydisc this application identifies the requested smooth analytification and etale-coordinate bridge with the existing PR196 supplier integrated through A0-extension.

Take its centred labelled polydisc chart and shrink away from the finitely many nonincident boundary components. Its coordinate equations give c_a(N_a intersect j_an(U(C)))=P_a^circ. Positivity of radii and b at most n are part of the chart, including n=b=0.

Restrict the inverse of c_a to P_a^circ, then use the inverse of the open-immersion identification to lift it uniquely to U(C). Injectivity of j_an proves the square and uniqueness; both inverse maps are analytic. The image is exactly j_an inverse-image of N_a.

Restrict the same maps when radii decrease, and reindex the first b coordinates when the incident labels are permuted. The square proves compatibility on overlaps. Every point of U(C) is in the image of a chart centred at its image in X(C), proving the cover; the construction chooses charts pointwise and asserts no uniform radius or finite subcover.
acceptance: The factorization is into the original U and uses its specified open immersion.
At a crossing remove every incident coordinate hyperplane, not just their common intersection.
The full neighbourhood chart includes boundary points; only the map ell_a has punctured domain.
The result provides the source input for Borel extension. Extension into an arithmetic quotient and algebraicity are separate consumer theorems.

api.name: borelSourceCharts.algebraicModel
api.statement: Expose the chosen X, j and labelled reduced D from snc-compactification, with X smooth projective and image j the complement of D. The choice is not canonical.

api.name: borelSourceCharts.fullChart
api.statement: Expose a in N_a, c_a(a)=0, positive radii, b at most n, the bijection between incident labels and the first b coordinates, and the full biholomorphism c_a.

api.name: borelSourceCharts.boundary
api.statement: For an incident label lambda_i, the points of D_lambda_i in N_a are exactly c_a inverse-image of z_i=0; every nonincident component misses N_a. Hence the image of N_a intersect j_an(U(C)) is P_a^circ.

api.name: borelSourceCharts.liftSquare
api.statement: There is a unique analytic ell_a:P_a^circ to U(C) satisfying j_an(ell_a(z))=c_a inverse(z). It is a biholomorphism onto j_an inverse-image of N_a, whose inverse is c_a composed with j_an.

api.name: borelSourceCharts.restrict
api.statement: If 0<sigma_i at most rho_i for every coordinate, use N_a prime=c_a inverse-image of P(sigma). The new ell_a is exactly the restriction of the old ell_a; successively shrinking twice equals the direct restriction.

api.name: borelSourceCharts.relabel
api.statement: Permuting the incident labels permutes the corresponding coordinates and radii in the full chart, and precomposes ell_a with the inverse coordinate permutation. Identity and composite permutations act accordingly.

api.name: borelSourceCharts.coverAndPullback
api.statement: The images of the ell_a cover U(C). For any analytic f:U(C) to a complex analytic target T, f composed with ell_a is analytic on P_a^circ; no extension of it is asserted by this API.

tests.name: BorelSourceChecks.point
tests.statement: For U=Spec C choose X=U, empty boundary and n=b=0. The empty coordinate product is a singleton and ell is the identity of that point, not a map with empty domain.

tests.name: BorelSourceChecks.projectiveInterior
tests.statement: For smooth projective U choose X=U and D empty. Every b is zero, so P^circ=P and ell is the full inverse chart. Artificially puncturing an ordinary coordinate would fail the boundary and image identities.

tests.name: BorelSourceChecks.affineLineInfinity
tests.statement: For U=A^1 in X=P^1, at infinity take w=1/t and |w|<rho. Here b=n=1 and ell(w)=1/w on 0<|w|<rho. The square lands in the actual affine t-line; zero belongs to the full chart but not to its lifted domain.

tests.name: BorelSourceChecks.torusCorner
tests.statement: For U=G_m squared in P^1 times P^1 at (0,0), the two incident boundary components are x=0 and y=0. The lifted domain is |x|<rho_1, |y|<rho_2, x nonzero and y nonzero. In particular (0,rho_2/2) is excluded although it is not the origin; at (0,1) only one factor is punctured after translating the other coordinate.

tests.name: BorelSourceChecks.preservedOpen
tests.statement: Let Y be the projective nodal cubic y^2 z=x^2(x+z) over C and U=Reg(Y). Its normalization P^1 is already a smooth SNC compactification: the two points above the node form its boundary and normalization restricts to an isomorphism with this exact U. The exported square factors through that isomorphism, and no point of U is deleted during compactification.

uses.how: For a holomorphic map on a quasi-projective source, restrict along ell_a before applying the independently proved arithmetic-quotient extension theorem; retain c_a on the full domain for that theorem’s conclusion.
